newsitem.title: USA: Sugen to start human trials for inhibitor.
newsitem.headline: Sugen to start human trials for inhibitor.

text.p: Sugen Inc said Tuesday it will begin human clinical studies of its Flk-1 TK angiogenesis inhibitor, an anti-metastasis and angiogenesis inhibitory treatment for solid tumor cancers, in mid-1997.

Sugen said in a release that the human clinical trials will test the inhibitor as a leading drug candidate, but added that final selection of a drug in this program may not be made until after initial human safety studies are complete.
Sugen said it expects to complete human safety studies by late 1997, and to move on to the first efficacy studies with the final drug candidate around the end of the year.

Stephen Evans-Freke, chairman and chief executive officer, said in the release that Sugen feels its "Flk-1 TK inhibitor program may become the most important program in (its) cancer development pipeline."

He added that animal studies have shown Flk-1 TK inhibitors to "block the growth of most solid tumors by angiogenesis inhibition, and in a metastatic animal model are able to prevent the spread of metastatic disease, the primary cause of death in many tumor types."
